headline: From genetic evidence to the next research question.
summary: Inspect an existing urate–gout finding, the SLC2A9 gene context, and the clinical history of a related urate-lowering treatment.
relationship_note: Febuxostat acts through xanthine oxidase inhibition. SLC2A9 is the genetic context here, not its drug target. Chronology does not establish that genetics drove the development decision.

sections.title: The question
sections.text: For urate and gout, what genetic evidence is already available, what gene context can we explain, and what can related clinical experience teach a research team?

sections.title: Retrieved genetic evidence
sections.text: The selected MVP1 record contains a positive pre-computed MR estimate for urate and gout. It was retrieved from MR-EVE, not recomputed here. Method and deposited dataset IDs remain attached to the original values.

sections.title: Gene context: SLC2A9
sections.text: The project atlas nominates SLC2A9 by proximity to rs938554. Separately, the 2008 paper provides human genetic and experimental evidence for urate transport. These are different evidence types and remain separately attributed.

sections.title: Related clinical experience
sections.text: Febuxostat lowers urate by inhibiting xanthine oxidase. It is included through the direct urate-lowering route, not as an SLC2A9-targeted treatment. CARES adds a cardiovascular-safety question in a specific gout population.

sections.title: What to check next
sections.text: A molecule-level genetic finding does not settle the safety of a particular drug. Review the MR design and missing diagnostics, then evaluate target mechanism, intended population and clinical endpoints separately.

sections.title: What remains uncertain
sections.text: Colocalisation and gene-QTL evidence were not queried in the selected baseline record. Nearest-gene assignment does not prove mediation. MR confidence-interval scale and level are unspecified in the source. This selected chronology is not an exhaustive clinical review.

events.title: SLC2A9, urate & gout
events.description: Human genetic associations and urate-transport experiments connect SLC2A9 with urate handling and gout.

events.title: Febuxostat approved
events.description: FDA approved febuxostat for hyperuricemia in adults with gout. It lowers urate through xanthine oxidase inhibition, a different mechanism from SLC2A9 transport.

events.title: CARES begins
events.description: Randomized febuxostat versus allopurinol cardiovascular-safety study in people with gout and cardiovascular comorbidities. Registry phase: Phase 3; official title: Phase 3B.
events.scope: Safety in the specified gout population

events.title: Benefits & risks diverge
events.description: The primary cardiovascular composite met noninferiority; cardiovascular and all-cause mortality were higher with febuxostat than allopurinol in CARES.

events.title: US boxed warning
events.description: FDA approved a boxed warning and a narrower indication following CARES. This is a safety-related label change, not a withdrawal of all urate-lowering treatments.

# MetaboCausal evidence card - urate x gout

## 1. Requested pair and resolved IDs

| Side | Asked for | Resolved label | Id | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Metabolite (exposure) | urate | 7,9-dihydro-1H-purine-2,6,8(3H)-trione | CHEBI:17775 | resolved from sample entry `urate\|gout` |
| Disease (outcome) | gout | gout | MONDO:0005393 | resolved from sample entry `urate\|gout` |

Synonyms handed to the metabolite-side tools (15): urate, 7,9-dihydro-1H-purine-2,6,8(3H)-trione, 2,6,8-trioxopurine, 2,6,8-trioxypurine, URIC ACID, purine-2,6,8(1H,3H,9H)-trione, Lithic acid, 2,6,8-trihydroxypurine (showing 8 of 15). Every match in this card is made on these strings, case-insensitively, not on the name as it was typed.

Synonyms handed to the disease-side tools (5): gout, chronic gout, gouty arthropathy, tophaceous disease, tophaceous gout. Every match in this card is made on these strings, case-insensitively, not on the name as it was typed.

One direction only: the metabolite is queried as the EXPOSURE and the disease as the OUTCOME. Nothing on this card is a statement about the reverse direction.

## 2. Evidence state and one-line verdict

**Verdict: State A - retrieved MR.** State A (retrieved MR): 22 estimate(s) carry a numeric effect size, uncertainty and p-value (retrieved MR (get_mr_result): 22). Retrieved from a published or pre-computed source, not computed here. Colocalisation: not queried in this run, so nothing here says whether the two GWAS share a causal variant. Any retrieved MR is retained without this additional supporting layer; colocalisation is not an inclusion requirement.

The state and the sentence above come from `classify.classify_state`, a pure function over this run's envelopes. No model wrote them and no model can change them.

The colocalisation clause is an evidence QUALIFIER: `get_colocalisation` runs after the classifier, its envelope is never passed to it, and no H4 on this card can move a pair between states A, B and C.

## 8. Caveats

**Run-level notes**

- rendered from data/demo_card_inputs.json, a CACHED SNAPSHOT of these envelopes taken 2026-09-10, not a live run.

**Tools that failed in this run**

- No tool returned an error envelope.

**Caveats declared by the tools, verbatim**

`get_mr_result` (EpiGraphDB MR-EVE):
- Retrieved from EpiGraphDB MR-EVE (OpenGWAS 2020-10-13 snapshot); automated MR labelled preliminary by the source. Not computed here. One direction only: the metabolite is queried as the EXPOSURE, never as the outcome, so nothing said here is a statement about the reverse direction.
- This MR-EVE snapshot does not return an SNP count, so nsnp is null on every row.
- n_estimates counts retrieved ROWS: 22 rows carry 13 distinct (b, se, pval). MR-EVE returns one row per MR method, and a study deposited under several OpenGWAS ids returns one row per id (ieu-a-1054 and ebi-a-GCST001790 are both the 2013 gout GWAS, n=69374), so identical numbers repeat. Never present this as a count of independent studies.
- Effect sizes are per unit of each exposure dataset's OWN scale and are not comparable across rows: ukb-d-30880_raw reports b per measured unit and ukb-d-30880_irnt b per SD of the same UKB measurement, an ~84x difference. This snapshot carries no `unit` for those datasets, so join exposure_id / outcome_id to the vocabulary (tools._traits) and print the dataset beside every number.
- moescore is MR-EVE's mixture-of-experts score (0-1) for how appropriate the automatically selected MR method was, and selection is its instrument-selection strategy (DF / HF). Neither is a significance measure, and neither is a confidence that the effect is causal.

`get_mqtl_instruments` (OpenGWAS (gwasinfo index + tophits)):
- Retrieved from OpenGWAS: the gwasinfo dataset index plus, per dataset, its pre-computed tophits. This is a feasibility report - which datasets exist and whether they carry instruments - and NOT an MR result. No estimate was computed here and nothing here says an effect exists.
- Dataset metadata is read from the local cache of https://api.opengwas.io/api/gwasinfo (data/gwasinfo.json, 50,056 datasets pulled 2026-09-10). No index request is sent per call; refresh it with tools._traits.build_opengwas_vocabulary().
- Capped: 22 dataset(s) measure this metabolite, only the 6 largest by sample size were queried (ieu-b-5137, ieu-a-1055, bbj-a-57, ieu-a-786, ieu-a-787, ieu-a-788); not queried: ieu-a-792, ieu-a-789, ieu-a-793, ieu-a-791, ieu-a-795, ukb-e-30880_CSA, met-a-345, ieu-a-794, ukb-e-30880_AFR, ieu-a-790, ieu-a-797, ieu-a-796, ukb-e-30880_EAS, ukb-e-30880_MID, ukb-d-30880_irnt, ukb-d-30880_raw. Raise max_datasets to see them.
- gwasinfo carries no platform field, so platform is INFERRED from the id batch prefix: met-a is the Metabolon-type mass-spectrometry panel (Shin 2014), met-c and met-d are Nightingale NMR (met-d being the UK Biobank release). Every other batch - met-b included, which is not a metabolite panel at all but Roederer 2015 immune-cell flow cytometry - is reported with platform null rather than guessed at.
- gws_hits counts OpenGWAS's own PRE-CLUMPED tophits at p < 5e-8: independent loci, not SNPs. The independence comes from that pre-computed set, built at OpenGWAS's own r2/kb defaults, and NOT from the clump flag this tool sends - measured 2026-09-10, met-d-Gly returns the same 49 rows with clump=1, with clump=0 and with no clump key at all, because preclumped defaults to 1. Clumping on the fly instead (preclumped=0, clump=1) gives a slightly different set: 52 rows in 6.7 s against 0.1 s. The p-value threshold IS applied on top of the pre-clumped set.
- F is the approximate per-SNP F statistic (beta/se)^2, arithmetic on the retrieved beta and se; weak_instruments counts hits with F < 10. It is NOT the first-stage F of a fitted MR, because no MR was fitted here, and a hit whose se is missing or zero gets no F at all. These betas also come from the same scan that selected the SNPs at p < 5e-8, so every F here is inflated by winner's curse - read it as an upper bound on instrument strength, not an estimate of it.
- Several datasets of one metabolite are not interchangeable: they are different assays on different scales - ieu-b-5137 (platform unknown, unit 'SD', n=440466) vs ieu-a-1055 (platform unknown, unit 'mg/dl', n=110347) vs bbj-a-57 (platform unknown, unit None, n=109029). Effect sizes across them are not comparable. Print platform / unit / sample_size beside every number and never merge them into one.
- A sex-stratified dataset or an interaction scan is not a main-effect exposure: an interaction beta measures how the SNP effect changes with the modifier, so F = (beta/se)^2 on it is not instrument strength. sex and note are reported per dataset for exactly this reason - three urate datasets (ieu-a-786/787/788) are otherwise identical rows. In this envelope: ieu-a-786 (sex 'Males and Females', note 'BMI by SNP interaction all; effect allele frequencies are missing'); ieu-a-787 (sex 'Males', note 'BMI by SNP interaction men; effect allele frequencies are missing'); ieu-a-788 (sex 'Females', note 'BMI by SNP interaction women; effect allele frequencies are missing').
- example_hits is the 5 strongest hits by p-value per dataset, not the whole instrument set; gws_hits is the full count.
- tophits answers an id it does not recognise with an empty list, exactly as it answers a real dataset that has no genome-wide hit. So gws_hits = 0 means "no LD-clumped hit at p < 5e-8 in this dataset" and never "this measurement has no genetic basis".

`find_outcome_datasets` (OpenGWAS (gwasinfo index + tophits)):
- Retrieved from OpenGWAS: the gwasinfo dataset index plus, per dataset, its pre-computed tophits. This is a feasibility report - which datasets exist and whether they carry instruments - and NOT an MR result. No estimate was computed here and nothing here says an effect exists.
- Dataset metadata is read from the local cache of https://api.opengwas.io/api/gwasinfo (data/gwasinfo.json, 50,056 datasets pulled 2026-09-10). No index request is sent per call; refresh it with tools._traits.build_opengwas_vocabulary().
- Ranking: datasets with a recorded sample_size first, then the curated repositories (ebi-, ieu-, finn-) ahead of the rest, then sample size descending. So this list is not a pure size ranking - a large dataset from another batch can sit below a smaller curated one - and the datasets gwasinfo records no sample_size for (every finn-b row) come last however big they are.
- Capped: 4 outcome dataset(s) match these synonyms, only the top 3 are returned (ebi-a-GCST90038687, ebi-a-GCST001790, ieu-a-1054); not returned: finn-b-M13_GOUT. Raise top_n to see them.
- Some of these are the SAME study deposited under more than one id (ebi-a-GCST001790 = ieu-a-1054): identical n, ncase and ncontrol. Count them once.
- ebi-a-GCST001790 and ieu-a-1054 (PMID 23263486) are deposits from the SAME publication (matching PMID) and are not independent outcome datasets - one can be a sub-stage of the other, so their sample sizes differ while the participants do not. Count the study once.
- ebi-a-GCST90038687: a UK Biobank deposit or a meta-analysis large enough (>= 250,000) that it very likely contains UK Biobank. gwasinfo records no cohort list, so this is a size-based flag, not a verified overlap. Sample overlap is NOT checked here and it is the first thing a two-sample MR reviewer asks. This tool sees one side of the pair at a time, so it cannot tell whether the exposure and outcome GWAS share participants. Overlapping samples bias two-sample MR towards the confounded observational estimate and inflate type-1 error. Check the cohort composition of BOTH datasets before any card says analysis-ready.
- gwasinfo stores some author / consortium names with broken non-ASCII escapes (ebi-a-GCST90038687, ebi-a-GCST001790; "K<c3><b6>ttgen A" is Kottgen A with an umlaut, "D<U+00F6>nerta<U+015F> HM" is Donertas HM). 1,357 of the 50,056 cached rows carry a "<U+00xx>" escape and 20 carry raw byte tokens. The string is reported exactly as the source wrote it - the damage is OpenGWAS's, not this tool's - so a renderer that wants a clean name has to repair it and say it did.
- gwasinfo records no population for ebi-a-GCST90038687 (it writes the literal "NA"), so the ancestry match against the exposure cannot be checked for those datasets from this envelope alone.
- ncase / ncontrol are reported exactly as gwasinfo wrote them. They are not always a study design: the ukb-e continuous panels carry ncase == sample_size and ncontrol == 0 on a blood measurement, and the finn-b datasets carry case and control counts but no sample_size at all.
- population is reported per dataset because it has to be checked against the exposure's population before any MR is run; this tool sees only one side of the pair and cannot check it for you.

`get_gwas_catalog` (GWAS Catalog (EBI) REST API):
- GWAS Catalog rows are curated trait-variant ASSOCIATIONS from published GWAS, not causal estimates: no MR, no instrument, no direction of causation. An odds ratio or beta here is the reported marginal association of one variant with the trait in that study's own scale and ancestry. Retrieved, not computed.
- Resolved through the ontology id: 'MONDO:0005393' -> MONDO_0005393 ('gout'). The trait name was not searched.
- This endpoint ignores `size` and `page` (measured 2026-09-10: identical 575 rows with and without size=5&page=0, `page` block null), so the full association set for the trait is transferred on every call and any cap below is applied here, after download, not by the server.
- Capped: 1420 association(s) were retrieved and the strongest 200 by p-value are kept; 1220 weaker row(s) were dropped after download.
- beta is the Catalog's own betaNum, which is an UNSIGNED MAGNITUDE - the direction lives in beta_direction ("increase" / "decrease"). Measured 2026-09-10 on rs1047891: 0 of 566 betaNum values are negative while 255 of them are "decrease". Reading beta alone gets the sign wrong on roughly 45% of rows. beta_signed is derived here for convenience (beta with the direction applied, null when the direction is missing); beta and beta_direction are the source's own fields.
- p-values reported as exactly 0 underflowed double precision in the source; the true exponent survives in pvalue_mantissa / pvalue_exponent (gout's strongest row is 1e-1421). Render those as "p ~ {mantissa}e{exponent} (reported 0)", never as p = 0, and note that ranking uses the mantissa/exponent pair for exactly this reason - sorting on the float would tie every underflowed row at the top.
- 21 of the 200 kept association(s) carry an author-reported gene entry; the rest name none, which is why mapped genes are fetched from the SNP resource separately.
- Mapped genes come from the SNP resource, one request per variant, and are capped at the strongest 10 variant(s) by p-value: 10 variant(s) queried out of 200 kept association(s), 72 gene row(s) returned.
- 2 of the 10 queried variant(s) returned no genomic context (chr4:88887327, chr4:89025241): the Catalog also writes positional ids such as chr4:88887327 and HGVS strings, which carry no gene annotation, and an unknown rsid answers 404.
- No distance cutoff was applied to mapped genes: rows span 0 to 146,949 bp from their variant (16 row(s) at distance 0) and include pseudogenes - rs1165151 returns histone pseudogenes out to 94,826 bp. Sort by distance and state the range before calling any of these an effector gene. Reported, not filtered.
- Mapped genes are listed once per annotation source, and the two sources disagree about distance (rs1165151 SLC17A3: 11,678 bp per Ensembl, 23,468 bp per NCBI). Both rows are kept exactly as retrieved, so the row count is not a gene count.
- `is_closest_gene` is the source's own per-source, per-direction flag (nearest upstream and nearest downstream, once for NCBI and once for Ensembl), so several genes carry it at one variant and the gene the variant sits INSIDE need not: at rs1165151 SLC17A1 is distance 0 with is_intergenic false and is_closest_gene false, while SLC17A3, SLC17A4 and LOC124901285 are all flagged closest. Do not read it as "the" nearest gene.
